title: Junk dealers' tin horns and Bugle Sam
summary: Memories of bottle dealers advertising with tin horns and Bugle Sam, who played blues on his bugle.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was going to ask some more when you were just a small boy. I think one night you were talking about the junk dealers and the old bottle rag man with their tin horns. Were you talking about that?
Yeah, they used to play as much on those tin horns as this guy, how do you call them, the bugle? Bugle Sam.
They played as much on those tin horns as the bugle Sam played on that bugle. Did he play like the old blues?
Absolutely. Did they do that to sort of advertise that they were coming up the street? That's right, yeah.
Some people know they were the bottle man. If they had any bottles to sell by, they'd get it on and they'd gather their bottles together.
Did they give any other cry along with it? No, no, that's all they used.
That's all they used. Just blowing that horn. They didn't yell out old bottle man. No bottle man, no. That's him with Bugle and Sam, he used to sell waffles. And that was his signal.
There's still another guy down there still does that.
He played the blues on it.
At least two years ago I was.
Yeah. Some of them would just blow a regular army bugle, you know, but Sam used to play the blues.
